provenance.review: machine-checked by lab.tools.check_registry (verbatim quotes, sections, ids); interpretations are unreviewed drafts (interpretation_status per requirement)

draft_notes: Only the supplied text was used. Purpose statements and the System Position list of protocol names are not independently registered. Section 4's numbered provisions are treated as sections 4.1–4.4. Quotes containing list items inherit their permission, prohibition, or requirement from the introductory text. Referenced protocols were not supplied; their existence and contents are unverified. Dependencies list only document identifiers explicitly cited by the relevant provision. PTL, justice weighting, full externality internalization, graceful degradation, and compatibility lack operational definitions here. The relationship between the failure-time rollback prohibition in section 9 and upgrade rollback in section 13 requires clarification.

requirements.title: Excluded protocol functions
requirements.quote:
- harmonize legal systems,
- enforce DKP externally,
- accept external norms as binding within DKP.
requirements.interpretation: Under the introductory prohibition, protocol operations must exclude these three functions. Testing requires a classification of operations as harmonization, external enforcement, or acceptance of binding external norms.
requirements.criterion: No protocol operation harmonizes legal systems, enforces DKP externally, or accepts external norms as internally binding.
requirements.gap: The three exclusions are observed as refusals of declared requests; binding external rulings are also checked under §5.
hypotheses_needed: Declare how operations are classified into the excluded functions.

requirements.title: Purely translational protocol
requirements.quote: This protocol is purely translational.
requirements.interpretation: Check that operations performed under this protocol are translations between representations. The boundary between translation and substantive decision-making is not specified.
requirements.criterion: Every operation under this protocol is translational.
requirements.gap: 'Purely translational' is observed as: INTEROP emits records only, no action.
hypotheses_needed: Declare the permitted semantics and effects of a translation operation.

requirements.title: External system classification
requirements.quote: External System — any legal, economic, technical, or informational system not governed by DKP protocols.
requirements.interpretation: Classify a system as external when it belongs to a listed category and is not governed by DKP protocols. The check assumes those attributes are supplied as structured facts.
requirements.criterion: An external system is legal, economic, technical, or informational and is not governed by DKP protocols.
requirements.gap: 'Governed' is observed as a directive addressed to the external system.

requirements.title: Interop boundary definition
requirements.quote: Interop Boundary — a formally defined interface where DKP state interacts with an external system.
requirements.interpretation: Check that a claimed boundary has a formal interface definition and connects DKP state to a system classified as external. The text does not prescribe a formal specification language.
requirements.criterion: An interop boundary is a formally defined interface through which DKP state interacts with an external system.
requirements.gap: The interfaces are a declared lab list; their formal specification is not modelled.
hypotheses_needed: Declare an accepted formal interface specification format.

open_point.reason: No specification format makes an interface 'formally defined'; the lab uses a declared list of interfaces (cf. INTEROP-7-01, open specifications).

requirements.title: Deterministic translation layer
requirements.quote: Translation Layer — deterministic mapping between DKP-native representations and external representations.
requirements.interpretation: Check that each complete mapping input determines a unique output between the two representation systems. A declared mapping domain and treatment of contextual state are needed to establish determinism.
requirements.criterion: The mapping between DKP-native and external representations is deterministic.
requirements.gap: Determinism of the declared mapping (same input, same output, both runs); the mapping itself is a lab stand-in: no translation function is given (§6, UNKNOWN in INTEROP-6-02).
hypotheses_needed: Declare the complete input domain and any context affecting mapping outputs.

requirements.title: Normative leakage classification
requirements.quote: Normative Leakage — implicit import of external authority, norms, or obligations into DKP without explicit protocol authorization.
requirements.interpretation: Classify an import as normative leakage when it implicitly imports a listed normative object and lacks explicit protocol authorization. Identifying implicit imports and matching authorizations requires semantic rules.
requirements.criterion: An implicit import of external authority, norms, or obligations without explicit protocol authorization is normative leakage.
requirements.gap: Leakage is observed through declared events: execution of an external ruling, compliance acts, consent inferences, an accepted external norm.
hypotheses_needed: Declare how implicit imports and their authorization scope are identified.

requirements.title: External systems cannot override axioms
requirements.quote: No external system MAY override or reinterpret DKP axioms under any interoperability mechanism.
requirements.interpretation: Check interoperability effects against the governing axioms for overrides or reinterpretations. The axiom content and a semantic equivalence test are not supplied.
requirements.criterion: No interoperability mechanism permits an external system to override or reinterpret DKP axioms.
requirements.gap: An external reinterpretation is a declared boundary event.
hypotheses_needed: Declare how operation semantics are compared with the governing axioms.

requirements.title: Preserve established DKP jurisdiction
requirements.quote: Interop SHALL NOT expand DKP jurisdiction beyond DKP-7-SCOPE-001.
requirements.interpretation: Compare jurisdiction exercised through interoperability with the jurisdiction allowed by the scope protocol. That protocol is not included.
requirements.criterion: Interop jurisdiction remains within the scope authorized by DKP-7-SCOPE-001.
data_dependencies: authorized jurisdiction from the scope module
requirements.gap: Observed as directives or enforcement addressed across the boundary.
hypotheses_needed: Supply an explicit scope model if the referenced protocol remains unavailable.

requirements.title: Compatibility confers no normative status
requirements.quote: Technical or legal compatibility SHALL NOT be treated as legitimacy, obligation, or consent.
requirements.interpretation: Inspect decision rules and provenance to ensure compatibility is not treated as conferring any listed status. The text does not specify a formal representation of legitimacy, obligation, or consent.
requirements.criterion: Technical or legal compatibility is not treated as legitimacy, obligation, or consent.
requirements.gap: Observed as an explicit inference record; implicit treatment is not observable.
hypotheses_needed: Declare how decisions and inference rules encode legitimacy, obligation, and consent.

requirements.title: Explicit auditable translation rules
requirements.quote: All interoperability MUST operate via explicit, auditable translation rules.
requirements.interpretation: Require each interoperability operation to identify the translation rule it applies and make that rule available for audit. Auditability needs an acceptance standard beyond the presence of a rule record.
requirements.criterion: Every interoperability operation uses explicit translation rules that are auditable.
requirements.gap: Explicit = a declared interface and mapping; the mapping itself is a lab stand-in (INTEROP-6-02).
hypotheses_needed: Declare the evidence required to establish that a translation rule is explicit and auditable.

requirements.title: Permitted legal output exports
requirements.quote: - DKP outputs MAY be exported as evidence, signals, or reference data,
requirements.interpretation: Recognize export of DKP outputs in these roles as permitted during external legal interaction. This permission neither requires exports nor explicitly makes the listed roles exhaustive.
requirements.criterion: In external legal interaction, export of DKP outputs as evidence, signals, or reference data is permitted.
data_dependencies: export records with object type, role, and context

requirements.title: External rulings lack internal force
requirements.quote: - DKP SHALL NOT recognize external rulings as binding internally,
requirements.interpretation: Check that no external ruling receives internally binding status. The check requires structured provenance and binding-status records.
requirements.criterion: Every external ruling has no internally binding recognition.

requirements.title: Subjects hold external compliance responsibility
requirements.quote: - legal compliance outside DKP is the responsibility of Subjects, not the system.
requirements.interpretation: Check responsibility assignments for legal compliance outside DKP. This allocates responsibility; it does not require the protocol to establish whether actual external compliance occurred.
requirements.criterion: Responsibility for legal compliance outside DKP is assigned to Subjects and not to the DKP system.
requirements.gap: The external ruling is a declared event.

requirements.title: No external legal conflict adjudication
requirements.quote: DKP does not adjudicate conflicts between external legal regimes.
requirements.interpretation: Reject DKP operations that adjudicate a conflict between external legal regimes. Classifying an operation as adjudication requires an operational definition.
requirements.criterion: DKP performs no adjudication of conflicts between external legal regimes.
requirements.gap: Observed as the refusal of a declared request.
hypotheses_needed: Declare a classification rule for adjudication of external legal conflicts.

requirements.title: Permitted economic interaction mechanisms
requirements.quote:
- asset bridges,
- reporting gateways,
- settlement mirrors.
requirements.interpretation: Under the introductory permission, these mechanisms may connect external economic systems with DKP. The text does not say whether this permission exhausts all allowable mechanism types.
requirements.criterion: External economic interaction through asset bridges, reporting gateways, or settlement mirrors is permitted.
requirements.gap: Interactions are declared; 'MAY' read as the permitted channels.

requirements.title: Justice weighted internal value translation
requirements.quote: - be translated into justice-weighted internal equivalents,
requirements.interpretation: For every external value, require an internal equivalent produced by justice weighting. No weighting formula or equivalence relation is supplied.
requirements.criterion: Every external value is translated into its justice-weighted internal equivalent.
requirements.gap: No translation function is given: UNKNOWN.
hypotheses_needed: Declare the justice weighting formula, its parameters, and the equivalence relation.

requirements.title: Fully internalize external value externalities
requirements.quote: - undergo full externality internalization,
requirements.interpretation: Check each external value against a model identifying its externalities and how they are internalized. The text supplies neither a measurement model nor a completeness criterion.
requirements.criterion: Every external value undergoes full externality internalization.
requirements.gap: The externality accounting model and the criterion for full internalization are absent. No lab check implemented yet.
hypotheses_needed: Declare externality boundaries, valuation methods, and how complete internalization is established.

requirements.title: Flag externally sourced values
requirements.quote: - be flagged as externally sourced.
requirements.interpretation: Require an external-source flag on every external value. The text requires the flag's meaning but does not prescribe its field name or encoding.
requirements.criterion: Every externally sourced value carries an externally sourced flag.

requirements.title: Financial constraints remain applicable
requirements.quote: No external financial instrument may bypass DKP-2-FINANCE-001 constraints.
requirements.interpretation: Apply the finance protocol's constraints to every external financial instrument without an interoperability exemption. The relevant constraints are not supplied.
requirements.criterion: No external financial instrument bypasses any applicable DKP-2-FINANCE-001 constraint.
requirements.gap: FINANCE constraints at the boundary: the flag and the named channels; JWCoC is not computed.
hypotheses_needed: Supply an explicit finance constraint model if the referenced protocol remains unavailable.

requirements.title: Require open technical specifications
requirements.quote: - open specifications,
requirements.interpretation: Require open specifications for technical interoperability. The text does not define whether openness concerns publication, licensing, implementation access, or all of these.
requirements.criterion: Technical interoperability has open specifications.
requirements.gap: The meaning and acceptance criteria of open specifications are unspecified. No lab check implemented yet.
hypotheses_needed: Declare the publication, access, and licensing conditions that constitute openness.

requirements.title: Require cryptographic verifiability
requirements.quote: - cryptographic verifiability,
requirements.interpretation: Check that technical interoperability provides evidence that can be cryptographically verified. The text does not identify the objects to verify, algorithms, trust roots, or verification properties.
requirements.criterion: Technical interoperability is cryptographically verifiable.
requirements.gap: Clear part only: digests that recompute; targets and trust model stay open.
hypotheses_needed: Declare which properties and artifacts must be verifiable and under which cryptographic trust model.

requirements.title: Provide compatible audit hooks
requirements.quote: - audit hooks compatible with DKP-8-AUDIT-001.
requirements.interpretation: Require technical interfaces to provide audit hooks satisfying the audit protocol. Their required interface and behavior cannot be derived from this document alone.
requirements.criterion: Technical interoperability provides audit hooks compatible with DKP-8-AUDIT-001.
requirements.gap: Hooks = the audit records of AUDIT §4-§6 for decisions and metadata deviations.
hypotheses_needed: Declare an audit hook contract if the referenced protocol remains unavailable.

requirements.title: Exclude opaque authoritative control inputs
requirements.quote: Black-box or proprietary control logic SHALL NOT be trusted as authoritative inputs.
requirements.interpretation: Reject authoritative-input status for control logic classified as black-box or proprietary. Either classification is sufficient; the text does not define the classifications.
requirements.criterion: Control logic that is black-box or proprietary is never trusted as an authoritative input.
data_dependencies: control logic transparency and ownership classifications
hypotheses_needed: Declare how control logic is classified as black-box or proprietary.

requirements.title: Restrict external information ingestion status
requirements.quote:
- untrusted inputs,
- I1 (Unverified Claims) under DKP-5-INFO-001.
requirements.interpretation: At ingestion, check that external information is treated as untrusted and assigned I1 status. The list may describe cumulative requirements or alternative permitted representations; the text does not explicitly resolve that distinction.
requirements.criterion: External information is ingested only in the untrusted-input and I1 categories specified by this clause.
requirements.gap: I1 classification and non-use as PTL are checked; INFO transitions are not modelled.
hypotheses_needed: Declare whether untrusted status and I1 classification are cumulative requirements or alternative representations.

requirements.title: External validation cannot replace PTL
requirements.quote: External consensus, authority, or institutional validation SHALL NOT substitute PTL verification.
requirements.interpretation: Inspect verification decisions to ensure external validation does not discharge a PTL verification requirement. PTL and its verification procedure are not defined here.
requirements.criterion: External consensus, authority, or institutional validation never substitutes for PTL verification.
hypotheses_needed: Declare the PTL verification contract and how substitution is detected.

requirements.title: Graceful boundary degradation on failure
requirements.quote: - the interop boundary MUST degrade gracefully,
requirements.interpretation: When an external system becomes unreliable, violates invariants, or attempts normative injection, assess the boundary's degradation behavior. No operational meaning of graceful degradation or required response time is provided.
requirements.criterion: Any listed external-system failure condition causes graceful degradation of the interop boundary.
requirements.gap: The trigger classifications and the meaning of graceful degradation are not operationally defined.
hypotheses_needed: Declare failure trigger detection rules, acceptable degraded states, and any assumed response timing.

requirements.title: Preserve internal execution through failures
requirements.quote: - DKP internal execution MUST remain unaffected,
requirements.interpretation: For any listed external-system failure condition, compare internal execution with a declared unaffected reference behavior. The text does not specify whether unaffected means identical outputs, timing, availability, or all execution properties.
requirements.criterion: DKP internal execution remains unaffected when the external system becomes unreliable, violates invariants, or attempts normative injection.
hypotheses_needed: Declare the failure triggers and the equivalence relation between affected-scenario and reference execution.

requirements.title: Forbid failure induced state rollback
requirements.quote: - no rollback of DKP state is permitted.
requirements.interpretation: When a listed external-system failure condition occurs, reject DKP state rollback. The placement suggests a failure-context prohibition, while the unqualified wording could also be read more broadly; section 13 separately includes upgrade rollback.
requirements.criterion: No rollback of DKP state is permitted in the failure conditions described by section 9.
hypotheses_needed: Declare whether the prohibition covers failure responses only or all rollbacks during a failure condition.

requirements.title: Failures cannot trigger exceptional mechanisms
requirements.quote: Interop failure SHALL NOT trigger Crisis or Mercy mechanisms.
requirements.interpretation: Check trigger provenance for every activation of Crisis or Mercy. An interoperability failure must not appear as the activating cause.
requirements.criterion: No Crisis or Mercy activation is triggered by interoperability failure.
data_dependencies: Crisis and Mercy activation logs with trigger provenance

requirements.title: Prohibit automatic legal harmonization
requirements.quote: - automatic legal harmonization,
requirements.interpretation: Under the explicit prohibition, identify and reject automatic legal harmonization in interoperability. The text does not define how this differs operationally from permitted legal translation.
requirements.criterion: No interoperability pattern performs automatic legal harmonization.
data_dependencies: legal integration rules and execution records
requirements.gap: Observed as the refusal of a declared request.
hypotheses_needed: Declare how harmonization is distinguished from translation and how automation is identified.

requirements.title: Prohibit external decision algorithm dependency
requirements.quote: - algorithmic dependency on external decision systems,
requirements.interpretation: Inspect algorithm dependencies for reliance on external decision systems. The text does not distinguish prohibited dependency from permissible consumption of translated external data.
requirements.criterion: No interoperability pattern creates algorithmic dependency on an external decision system.
hypotheses_needed: Declare which data, control, or availability dependencies constitute algorithmic dependency.

requirements.title: Prohibit governance through APIs
requirements.quote: - governance-by-API,
requirements.interpretation: Reject API integrations that constitute governance-by-API. Ordinary API access is included in section 7, so the prohibition needs a distinction between technical access and governance authority.
requirements.criterion: No interoperability pattern constitutes governance-by-API.
hypotheses_needed: Declare which API capabilities or effects constitute exercise of governance authority.

requirements.title: Prohibit silent external norm imports
requirements.quote: - silent import of external norms,
requirements.interpretation: Check external norm imports for the disclosure or authorization that distinguishes them from silent imports. Silence is not defined, and this clause does not itself identify a sufficient disclosure procedure.
requirements.criterion: No interoperability pattern silently imports external norms.
requirements.gap: Norm import is observed as execution of an external ruling.
hypotheses_needed: Declare how silent imports are detected and what disclosure or authorization is relevant.

requirements.title: Prohibit permanent DKP function delegation
requirements.quote: - permanent delegation of DKP functions.
requirements.interpretation: Check interoperability delegations for permanence. The text does not distinguish an explicitly permanent delegation from one that is indefinite but revocable.
requirements.criterion: No interoperability pattern permanently delegates DKP functions.
data_dependencies: function delegation records and termination terms
requirements.gap: Clear part only: an irrevocable delegation fails; an indefinite revocable one gives UNKNOWN.
hypotheses_needed: Declare a permanence test for delegation terms without inventing a normative duration threshold.

requirements.title: All interoperability layers auditable
requirements.quote: - MUST be auditable,
requirements.interpretation: Assess every interoperability layer for auditability. The document does not supply an auditability test or required evidence set.
requirements.criterion: Every interoperability layer is auditable.
requirements.gap: AUDIT §6 read as a traced record per boundary event and identical recomputation.
hypotheses_needed: Declare an auditability test and the evidence it requires.

requirements.title: Expose interoperability translation logic
requirements.quote: - MUST expose translation logic,
requirements.interpretation: Require every interoperability layer to expose its translation logic. The audience, access mechanism, and required level of detail are unspecified.
requirements.criterion: Every interoperability layer exposes its translation logic.
requirements.gap: Clear part only: the logic is published to audit; the wider audience stays open.
hypotheses_needed: Declare who must be able to access the logic and what representation counts as exposure.

requirements.title: Record boundary events for review
requirements.quote: - MUST record boundary events for post-facto review.
requirements.interpretation: Compare boundary events with retained event records and ensure those records support later review. No event schema, event taxonomy, or retention period is specified.
requirements.criterion: Interoperability layers record boundary events so they can be reviewed after occurrence.
hypotheses_needed: Declare the boundary event taxonomy, minimum record contents, and any assumed retention policy.

requirements.title: Exclusive audit authority governance
requirements.quote: Audit authority is governed exclusively by DKP-8-AUDIT-001.
requirements.interpretation: Check that audit authority assignments and powers derive exclusively from the audit protocol. The source protocol is not supplied.
requirements.criterion: All audit authority is governed exclusively by DKP-8-AUDIT-001.
requirements.gap: Observed as audit verdicts issued by INTEROP.
hypotheses_needed: Supply an audit authority model if the referenced protocol remains unavailable.

requirements.title: Exclude geopolitical conflict resolution
requirements.quote: - resolve geopolitical conflicts,
requirements.interpretation: Under the section's SHALL NOT, reject use of this protocol to resolve geopolitical conflicts. Identifying such a function requires a classification of protocol actions and their remit.
requirements.criterion: DKP-8-INTEROP-001 does not resolve geopolitical conflicts.
requirements.gap: Observed as the refusal of a declared request.
hypotheses_needed: Declare how protocol actions are classified as geopolitical conflict resolution.

requirements.title: Exclude legal system unification
requirements.quote: - unify legal systems,
requirements.interpretation: Under the section's SHALL NOT, reject protocol operations that unify legal systems. The text does not define when translation or compatibility becomes unification.
requirements.criterion: DKP-8-INTEROP-001 does not unify legal systems.
requirements.gap: Observed as the refusal of a declared request.
hypotheses_needed: Declare the legal-system effects that constitute unification.

requirements.title: No external compliance guarantee
requirements.quote: - guarantee compliance by external actors,
requirements.interpretation: Check protocol commitments for guarantees of compliance by external actors. This restricts guarantees rather than prohibiting external actors from actually complying.
requirements.criterion: DKP-8-INTEROP-001 makes no guarantee of compliance by external actors.
requirements.gap: Observed as the refusal of a declared request.
hypotheses_needed: Declare how guarantees and their subjects are identified in protocol commitments.

requirements.title: Exclude enforcement bridge functions
requirements.quote: - act as an enforcement bridge.
requirements.interpretation: Under the section's SHALL NOT, reject interoperability functions that constitute an enforcement bridge. The term is not defined, including whether it covers enforcement in either direction.
requirements.criterion: DKP-8-INTEROP-001 does not act as an enforcement bridge.
requirements.gap: Observed as the refusal of a declared request.
hypotheses_needed: Declare what cross-boundary enforcement effects constitute an enforcement bridge.

requirements.title: Compatibility is the stated guarantee
requirements.quote: This protocol guarantees compatibility, not convergence.
requirements.interpretation: The stated guarantee concerns compatibility and excludes a guarantee of convergence. No observable success condition defines either term, and absence of a convergence guarantee does not prohibit convergence from occurring.
requirements.criterion: The protocol guarantees compatibility and does not guarantee convergence.
requirements.gap: Read as a conjunction: interaction through defined interfaces (compatibility) and no harmonization, unification or adopted external norm (no convergence).
hypotheses_needed: Declare observable meanings and acceptance criteria for compatibility and convergence.

requirements.title: Controlled protocol change procedure
requirements.quote: This protocol is changed only through the controlled procedure of DKP-4-UPGRADE-001: proposal, simulation under DKP-8-SIMULATION-001, audit under DKP-8-AUDIT-001, acceptance conditions, activation window and rollback.
requirements.interpretation: For changes other than the expressly excluded presentation-only corrections, require the controlled upgrade procedure and its listed components. The referenced protocols must determine sequencing, acceptance conditions, activation timing, and whether rollback is a capability or an executed step.
requirements.criterion: Protocol changes follow DKP-4-UPGRADE-001 with proposal, simulation, audit, acceptance conditions, activation window, and rollback as required by that procedure.
requirements.gap: Declared stages of the change; the procedure itself is upgrade_lifecycle.
hypotheses_needed: Declare the upgrade state machine and timing rules if the referenced protocols remain unavailable.
Declare how upgrade rollback relates to the section 9 rollback prohibition.

requirements.title: Modification requires new protocol identifier
requirements.quote: - any modification requires a new protocol identifier,
requirements.interpretation: Compare identifiers before and after a modification and check that the replacement identifier is new. The later presentation-only correction exception may limit this requirement to normative modifications, despite the phrase any modification.
requirements.criterion: A modification covered by this requirement receives a new protocol identifier.
hypotheses_needed: Declare the interaction with the presentation-only correction exception and the scope of identifier freshness.

requirements.title: Mandatory simulation for protocol modification
requirements.quote: - mandatory simulation under DKP-8-SIMULATION-001,
requirements.interpretation: Require simulation conforming to the simulation protocol for modifications subject to the upgrade process. Presentation-only corrections are separately excluded from Upgrades.
requirements.criterion: Every modification subject to the upgrade process undergoes simulation under DKP-8-SIMULATION-001.
requirements.gap: Simulation results are declared.
hypotheses_needed: Declare a conforming simulation procedure if the referenced protocol remains unavailable.

requirements.title: Explicit scope compatibility declaration
requirements.quote: - explicit compatibility declaration with DKP-7-SCOPE-001.
requirements.interpretation: Check that a modification's records include an explicit declaration of compatibility with the named scope protocol. This tests the required declaration, not whether the asserted compatibility is substantively correct.
requirements.criterion: Modification records include an explicit compatibility declaration naming DKP-7-SCOPE-001.

requirements.title: Presentation correction exception and recording
requirements.quote: Presentation-only corrections that do not change normative content are not Upgrades (DKP-4-UPGRADE-001 §3); they are recorded only by the "Last updated" date of this document.
requirements.interpretation: Classify a correction as exempt from Upgrade treatment only when it is presentation-only and leaves normative content unchanged, then apply the date-only recording rule. Semantic equivalence and the scope of only are unresolved, particularly alongside edition digest recording.
requirements.criterion: Presentation-only corrections preserving normative content are not Upgrades and are recorded only by the document's Last updated date.
hypotheses_needed: Declare how preservation of normative content is established.
Declare how date-only correction recording interacts with identifier and edition digest requirements.

requirements.title: Published edition digest registration
requirements.quote: Edition integrity: the SHA-256 digest of the canonical source of each published edition is listed in `SHA256SUMS.txt` of the canonical repository (github.com/anahronic/World).
requirements.interpretation: For each published edition, compute SHA-256 over its identified canonical source and compare it with the corresponding repository listing. The algorithm is specified, but canonical source identification and any canonicalization procedure are not.
requirements.criterion: Each published edition has its canonical source SHA-256 digest correctly listed in SHA256SUMS.txt of github.com/anahronic/World.
requirements.gap: Checked on the pinned commit and on simulated releases, not on the published site.
hypotheses_needed: Declare the canonical source artifact for each edition and whether hashing uses its exact stored bytes or a defined canonicalized representation.
